method: read what host/ and tests/ do with each command, and whether a control opcode covers it, rather than reasoning from the letters

O.role: console FALLBACK inside measure.occupancy(); OP_OCCUPANCY is tried first

l_read.role: test_load.py's two-transport agreement test reads BOTH by construction

W.opcode: CTL_OP_GEN 0x0010, in lib/due_shared/src/ctl.c - shared source, so Track C has it if it links the shared parser, which invariant 3 says it does. Zero length reads, a full payload writes and reads back.

no_control_equivalent.=1l: clear the load maximum - a WRITE. OP_LOAD reads only. A maximum cannot be differenced, so max_us is meaningless without a clear and the console is the only writer.

unverified.t: h_ratesweep. OP_RATE_TRACE is the consumed-buffer timestamp trace and the handler runs a sweep; they look different but cmd_ratesweep was not read. Treat as unchecked.

means: The port list is six writes, not ten commands. Three of the ten are host-side transport choices rather than Track C work: O is a fallback, l-read is a test that needs both transports, and W has a shared-source control opcode Track C already has.
invariant_8: It governs what is READ while the sample path runs, so it answers O and l and has nothing to say about the other eight, which are commands that make the device do something. That is probably why the ruling felt larger than it is.
evidence_asymmetry: The three positives were confirmed by reading the implementations. The 'none found' rows are a grep over opcode names and the shared dispatcher - a capability under a differently named opcode would not show. The negatives are weaker than the positives, which matters before this is treated as the port list rather than a starting point for one.
not_a_ruling: The ruling is mac-bench's. This is what the ten commands are, not what should be done about them.

needs_nothing.O: OP_OCCUPANCY preferred; console is the fallback
needs_nothing.W: CTL_OP_GEN, shared source - Track C has the opcode

one_table_entry_body_already_available.J: gen_set_sync() - drivers/gen.h; invariant 4 says Track C links identical driver code

t_resolved: Flagged unverified last time because OP_RATE_TRACE looked like it might cover it. It does not - but console_cmd_rate_sweep is already shared source, so the answer came out the same way for a different reason.
means_v2: Three commands need nothing, four need one line in Track C's table because the body is already shared or in drivers/, and four are genuine work because their bodies live in Track B's main.c - the one file per track invariant 3 does not share. Ten unbound-and-used commands was never ten pieces of work.
suggested_shape: The four real ports are all Track B main.c locals, and three of the four are debug instruments rather than capabilities - the class invariant 7 already carves out as debug-only and unreachable on the deployed path. So the ruling may be 'does Track C need Track B's debug instruments at all', which an owner can answer without a porting estimate.
